title: The Dialect Deadlock
logline: An obsolete regional idiom in a century-old station treaty leaves two allied administrators convinced the other is legally responsible for an expensive gate relay overhaul.

roles.description: A philologist who uncovered the root grammatical ambiguity in the founding charter.
Administrator of the outer relay station; operating on a shoestring budget and convinced the inner habitat is cheating them.
Auditor for the prosperous inner ring station; convinced their translation of the charter is legally watertight.
The original hand-illuminated parchment deed signed by the founding colonial captains.
The decaying communication and navigation relay station stranded between the two habitats.

public_situation: Maintenance on the vital midpoint navigation relay has halted because two allied stations are locked in a diplomatic standoff over who must pay for replacement couplers.
private_truth: The archaic charter phrase for 'shared upkeep' used a colonial term that meant 'whichever party is closest' in one dialect and 'whichever party has greater wealth' in the other.

beats.public_change: The midpoint navigation relay switches to low-power standby as maintenance funding expires.

missions.reason: The archivist needs a neutral ship to scan the physical cornerstone at the relay station where the original treaty clause was engraved in copper.
missions.private_fact: She already suspects the original phrasing was a deliberately vague compromise penned by a colonial scribe trying to stop a brawl.

beats.public_change: Both station offices dispatch competing legal summonses claiming breach of contract.

missions.reason: The governor hires an outside courier to deliver the certified colonial grammar lexicon to the relay tribunal before the bailiff files an eviction writ.
missions.private_fact: His station has already spent its maintenance contingency on an emergency solar array repair and cannot pay a single credit.

beats.public_change: The relay transformer sparks out, cutting navigational telemetry across the sector channel.

missions.reason: The bailiff contracts a hauler to purchase replacement transformers on the open market, seeking to bill the cost to whichever party loses the charter tribunal.
missions.private_fact: The inner station's legal department advised him that losing the grammatical case would void twelve other trade agreements.

player_choice.prompt: The archivist presents three interpretations of the treaty to the pilot, asking which version should be submitted as the binding arbitration record.

options.label: Certify an equal fifty-fifty liability clause
Certify the wealth-based clause binding the inner habitat
Declare the archaic treaty hopelessly void

resolutions.reached_by: The pilot submits the equal-liability translation, forcing a joint compromise.
resolutions.summary: Both habitats sign an updated joint protocol. {role:relay_spire} resumes telemetry, and {role:lexical_archivist} is appointed treaty secretary.

consequences.public_summary: A pilot helped archivists untangle an old dialect knot, saving an allied relay accord.

resolutions.reached_by: The pilot certifies the wealth-based colonial clause, forcing the inner station to pay.
resolutions.summary: {role:inner_bailiff} pays for the overhaul under protest. {role:outpost_governor} avoids bankruptcy, but inner-ring trade tariffs spike in retaliation.

consequences.public_summary: An ancient dialect ruling forced the inner habitat to swallow the full bill for a border spire.

resolutions.reached_by: The pilot declares the treaty void due to linguistic ambiguity.
resolutions.summary: The mutual-aid pact collapses. {role:relay_spire} is abandoned to private salvage, and navigation fees triple across the sector.
Neither station yields before the deadline. {role:relay_spire} suffers catastrophic core burnout, cutting the transit corridor indefinitely.

loose_threads.detail: A junior clerk in the inner archives notes that five pages of the original charter lexicon were rebound in calfskin bearing a bank's watermark.
The relay tribunal register records that both stations have paid annual retainer fees to the same consulting notary for thirty years.

radio_hooks: Navigation telemetry flickers as midpoint relay maintenance dispute reaches arbitration tribunal.
Outer habitat leaders accuse inner ring bailiffs of deliberate bad-faith grammar readings.
Antiquarian scholars summoned to decipher century-old settlement charter clauses in {system}.

voice_direction.lexical_archivist: Pedantic, quiet, and speaks with rhythmic pauses like reading an ancient manuscript. Avoids taking political sides.
voice_direction.outpost_governor: Gruff, defensive, and talks fast to hide how desperate his finances are. Never mentions his station's broken solar banks.
voice_direction.inner_bailiff: Smug, formal, and over-enunciates legal syllables. Never admits that his superiors want an excuse to dissolve the treaty.
